alignments.note: Construct noun with a supplied the; the article present in the chain stands on the rectum's own word, so nothing is fronted (rule 29's arthrous case).
Article on the rectum takes the the standing before its own word (rule 29).
Rectum takes the relational of (rule 19); the unit is discontinuous around the article's the (rule 25).

Preposition heading the predicate -> in. The clause's copula goes to the written copular pronoun rather than here, since a present morpheme takes its English before a supplied reading does; the competing reading puts the copula on this preposition under rule 49.
The assimilated article is a real token and takes the written the (rule 12).
The copular pronoun of the tripartite nominal clause takes the English is; the competing reading puts the copula on the prepositional predicate under rule 49 and leaves this pronoun unrepresented.
Verb with its auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb (rule 24).
le before the infinitive construct takes the written to (rule 52).
Light verb plus complement: make atonement heads on the complement (rule 44).

The copular pronoun is rendered by the cleft's it is, headed on the pronoun that realizes its lexeme; the copula stays with this written morpheme rather than being supplied to the predicate, as in the verse's first clause.

The cleft relative that subordinates a finite clause to a written antecedent; no relative morpheme stands in the clause and rule 46 governs only a headless one, so rules 46 and 55 leave it added. The competing reading takes the whole cleft frame it is ... that as one rendering of the copular pronoun.

The preposition alone is rendered by the compound by reason of, a single rendering of which no morpheme owns a part (rule 30), headed on the content word by rule 24's own example. Corrected: the assimilated article is not folded in here, because the ASV writes a the of its own before life, which is English spent on that one morpheme and defeats rule 30's one-rendering condition.
The assimilated article is a real token and takes the written the standing before its own noun (rule 12); a present article morpheme takes its English before a supplied one does (rules 29 and 47).
Noun -> life; its determiner is the article's own, not a supplied one.
Light verb plus complement: maketh atonement heads on atonement (rule 44).

review_notes: Corrected: ba-nephesh is divided as by reason of (the preposition, headed on reason) + the (the assimilated article) + life (the noun). The accepted alignment folded the article into the compound preposition's fused unit and then treated the ASV's the as supplied on the noun, which contradicts rule 12 and rule 30's own limit, since the written the before life is English spent on that one morpheme.

Both copular pronouns take the ASV's is, on the principle that a present morpheme takes its English before a supplied reading does; the competing reading puts the first is on the prepositional predicate under rule 49.
The cleft that of it is the blood that maketh atonement is added under rule 55, since the antecedent is written and no relative morpheme stands in the clause.
